description.narrative:
CODESRIA:s strategiska plan 2023-2027: "The Social Sciences in Africa in a Context of Global Transitions and Transformations" bygger vidare på den tidigare (för närvarande finansierad av Sida) genom att identifiera och fokusera på fyra tematiska områden och fyra genomgripande ämnen.
De fyra tematiska områdena inkluderar:
- Högre utbildningsdynamik i Afrika
- Staten och demokratiseringen i Afrika: trender och framtidsutsikter
- Transformationer i afrikanska ekonomier
- Människors interaktion med miljön i Afrika
De fyra övergripande frågorna inkluderar:
- Historia, minne och arkiv
- Jämställdhetsfrågor
- Generationer
- Landsbygd och urbanitet
Det övergripande målet för den strategiska planen 20232027 är att säkerställa en ökning av afrikanska bidrag till uppgiften att förstå, tolka och adressera de viktigaste utmaningarna på den afrikanska kontinenten. Specifika mål inkluderar:
1: Öka produktionen av kvalitativ och relevant samhällsvetenskaplig forskning som tar upp de prioriterade forskningsområdena i programcykeln 20232027. 2: Förbättra engagemanget i samhällsvetenskaplig forskning producerad av afrikaner. 3: Förbättra kapaciteten hos afrikanska universitet att utbilda doktorander. 4: Stärka förmågan till institutionell effektivitet och ansvar. 5: Öka CODESRIA:s jämställdhetsarbete.
Den strategiska planens förändringsteori (ToC) relaterar hur de planerade insatserna kan katalysera förändringar kopplat till det som identifieras som en av de största utmaningarna för samhällsvetenskaplig forskning på den afrikanska kontinenten: att afrikanska röster inte bidrar till att förstå och ta itu med de utmaningar som kontinenten står inför.
I detta avseende föreslår ToC att aktiviteter som - stödjer afrikanska forskare; underlättar kunskapsproduktion och dess spridning; stärker kapaciteten för högre utbildning; och stärker CODESRIA:s institutionella kapacitet och jämställdhetsintegrering - leder till en ökning av afrikanska bidrag för att förstå och hantera de utmaningar som den afrikanska kontinenten står inför.

Insatsen avser stödja Council for the Development of Social Science Research in Africa, CODESRIA, och dess genomförande av den strategiska planen för 2017-2021 "Reaching new frontiers in social science research and knowledge production for African transformation and development". Det övergripande målet i den strategiska planen för 2017-2021 är "Att främja samhällsvetenskaplig forskning och forskning inom humaniora som fokuserar på de prioriterade utvecklingsutmaningarna i Afrika". För att nå detta mål organiserar CODESRIA en mängd olika kärnaktiviteter inom tre tematiska forskningsområden. CODESRIAs globala budget är fördelad på fem mål; (1) Forskningsprogrammet 20%, (2) Publikationer och spridning 5%, (3) Akademisk frihet och förbättrad styrning och kapacitet av universitet 1.6%, (4) Forskningskapacitet 25%, (5) Organisationsutveckling och finansiering 35%. Sidas bedömning är att de planerade aktiviteterna för att genomföra och nå målen i den strategiska planen och öka kunskapsproduktionen inom de tre tematiska forskningsområdena är väl motiverade och genomförbara.
CODESRIA är ett panafrikanskt forskningsråd och nätverk inom samhällsvetenskap och humaniora. Huvudkontoret, det vill säga sekretariatet med ansvar för implementering av programmen är lokaliserat i Senegals huvudstad Dakar. CODESRIAs juridiska status är enskild organisation med värdlandsavtal med Senegal. Enligt värdlandsavtalet ges skattefrihet och straffimmunitet till CODESRIA som organisation och vissa av de anställda. Detta innebär att CODESRIA är skyddat från politiska och polisiära ingripanden vilket är ett skydd för CODESRIA men det innebär också en risk för Sida. Risken ligger i att vid eventuell upptäckt av korruption är enskilda personer skyddade från åtal och om krav på återbetalning av medel inte accepteras av CODESRIA kan Sida inte ta hjälp av polis och domstolsväsendet i Senegal. Sida bedömer dock att risken att en sådan tvist skulle uppstå är liten.
Sida har stött CODESRIA sedan 1977 med basstöd och riktat stöd och varit en av de viktigaste givarna tillsammans med Norad och Danida. Dessvärre tar Danidas avtal med CODESRIA slut 2016. Danida har pågrund av förändrade politiska prioriteringar dragit ned på stöd till forskningssamarbete och det finns ingen kännedom om planerat fortsatt stöd. Norads avtal om programstöd till CODESRIA tar slut i slutet av 2016. Även Norad har genomgått förändringar och väntat på en ny strategi från norska regeringen för forskningssamarbetet. Norad har inte kunnat ge någon vidare information om ungefärligt belopp eller typ av stöd vid en eventuell fortsättning. Sidas basstöd har därmed blivit ännu mer viktigt för CODESRIA för att kunna täcka löner, hyra och de viktigaste kärnaktiviterna. Sidas bedömning är att den osäkra finansiella situationen kring basstöd är den största risken på längre sikt för genomförandet av den strategiska planen och den grundforskning CODESRIA stödjer eftersom CODESRIA blir sårbar vid en eventuell minskning av Sidas stöd.
Vid sekretariatet arbetar ca 30 personer från hela kontinenten och den nuvarande chefen vid sekretariatet är Executive Secretary, Ebrima Sall. Salls kontrakt går ut under våren 2017 och rekrytering av en ny chef pågår. CODESRIA styrs av två separata organ, generalförsamlingen, (the General Assembly) som möts vart tredje år vid en stor konferens och består av CODESRIAs institutionella och individuella medlemmar. Mellan generalförsamlingens möten styrs organisationen av ett arbetsutskott (Executive Committee) bestående av 10 valda medlemmar. Arbetsutskottet träffas minst två gånger per år. Sidas bedömning är att CODESRIA är en i huvudsak väletablerad och välfungerande organisation men det har sedan en tid tillbaka funnits friktion och samarbetsproblem mellan sekretariatet och den exekutiva kommittéen. En annan svaghet i organisationen är bristande resurser och intresse för det löpande arbetet med resultatuppföljning, styrning och planering (M&E). En konsekvens av det är förseningar i årlig rapportering och i leverans av annat material (till exempel inför beredningen av nytt avtal) till Sida och andra givare. CODESRIA har på eget initiativ genomfört tre interna granskningar i syfte att reformera och effektivisera verksamheten och organisationen.
Sida kommer noggrant följa reformarbetet och på olika sätt stödja det i syfte att öka CODESRIAs effektivitet, relevans och hållbarhet. Sida kommer under avtalsperioden att genomföra två utvärderingar och en granskning av intern styrning och kontroll. Den första utvärderingen är en sedan tidigare planerad utvärdering av kärnaktiviteterna som blivit försenad. Denna tillsammans med granskningen av intern styrning och kontroll kommer utgöra underlag för en halvtidsöversyn då Sida tar ställning till CODESRIAs reformarbete. Ett krav för en sjätte utbetalning är att Sida godkänner CODESRIAs svar (management response) och uppdatering av handlingsplanen för reformprocessen. Den andra utvärderingen kommer att ske i slutet av programperioden och bedöma genomförandet av den strategiska planen och om resultat uppnåts som förutsatt.
Sidas bedömning är att CODESRIAs arbete med att stödja relevant forskning inom samhällsvetenskap och humaniora och utveckling av forskningskapacitet på den Afrikanska kontinenten är viktigt och relevant i den afrikanska vetenskapliga kontexten med få forskningsuniversitet och begränsade resurser till forskning.

The Council for the Development of Social Sxcience Research in Africa (CODESRIA) is a pan-African social science research organization. CODESRIA supports research and knowledge production in Africa. Besides, the organisation is involved in spreading research and publications on Africa. Sida gives core support to CODESRIA.

description.narrative:
The annual narrative report for 2023 documents the following Actual Progress towards results:
Specific Objective 1: Increase the production of quality and relevant social research addressing the priority research areas of the 20232027 programme cycle.
Meaning-Making Research Initiatives (MRI): The first cohort of MRI calls (covering the 2023-2024 period) were advertised in November 2023, with submission deadlines set for February 20th 2024. Three MRI calls, i.e MRI General (Individual and Group grants), MRI Advanced Senior Research Fellowships, and MRI Special Call for Female scholars, were launched in three languages - English, French, and Portuguese.
The 16th CODESRIA General Assembly (GA): Held in December 2023, the 16th GA included approximately 350 participants from 42 countries within Africa and beyond. Held under the overarching theme of The Social Sciences and Pandemics in Africa, the GA call for applications attracted the submission of 506 abstracts, of which 305 were accepted for development into full papers following a blind peer review process.
Specific Objective 2: Enhance engagement with social research produced by Africans.
Publications: CODESRIA disseminates its research including work produced by others in and on Africa to a wider audience through its publications and dissemination programme (PDP). By the end of 2023, the Council had published all issues of CODESRIA Bulletin. The Council also published nine (9) articles in the CODESRIA Bulletin Online Series. Two (2) of the Bulletins were special issues dedicated to the 16th CODESRIA GA and to the 50th Anniversary of CODESRIA. The Council also published all issues of Africa Development. The issues of Journal of Higher Education in Africa, vol. 21, no. 1 and no. 2, 2023 are all in final stages of production and will be released in early 2024. A total of seven (7) books were published during the period with two (2) of these being formally launched at events that drew both scholars and policy practitioners. The two books are Home and Exile: Forced Migrations and South Sudanese Refugees in Kenyas Kakuma Refugee Camp by Barrack O. Muluka and The Concept of Human Rights in Africa (Second Edition) by Issa Shivji. PDP currently has seven (7) manuscripts at an advanced stage of production including four (4) that are awaiting proof-reading and indexing. An additional three (3) book manuscripts that have been either copyedited or typeset are set for publication in 2024.
Dissemination efforts: CODESRIA seeks to bring the work it supports to a wide scholarly and policy audience so as to influence scholarship, teaching and policy in and on Africa. The following are some of the dissemination efforts that CODESRIA undertook during 2023:
The library continued to provide key contributions to the scientific activities of the Council, such as thematic bibliographies for the Gender and the Democratic Governance Institute reflections meetings in June and July; a bibliography on reparations that fed into the Executive Secretarys (ES) proposal to the Open Society Foundation in April; and an annotated bibliography on Higher Education Dynamics in Africa for the last 30 years (from 1990-2023) for the Training, Grants and Fellowships (TGF) Programme.
The CODESRIA Documentation and Information Centre (CODICE) continued to offer services based on Internet and databases searches, and generated subject bibliographies upon requests from users external to CODESRIA Secretariat.
Outreach and engagement: CODESRIA made efforts to engage a diversity of scholarly and policy actors to project the Councils image and that of the African social science and humanities community. This effort included CODESRIA staff participating in meetings and activities led by other organizations. Some of the key meetings and engagements attended by staff include:
The Association of African Universities (AAU) led consultative meeting on the development of an Africa-centred guiding framework for transformative global North & Africa research collaborations. This initial meeting was held in Accra, Ghana on January 26, 2023.
The 6th ACSS Conference and General Assembly of the ACSS held in Beirut, Lebanon from May 25-28, 2023 and participated in a panel on Theorizing from the South: Transregional Perspectives. The meeting provided an opportunity to advance discussions on an Afro-Arab Initiative between CODESRIA and ACSS.
On September 1st 2023, CODESRIA senior staff, under the request of the South African Embassy, held a meeting with their diplomatic staff to discuss the political developments in West Africa and Niger crisis.
The Coalition for Dialogue on Africa (CoDA)s high level dialogue meeting on Africa in the Changing World Order held in Nairobi, Kenya on 27th & 28th October 2023.
The Norad NORHED weeks held in October 2023 at the University of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania and Makerere University, Uganda.
The Development Leaders Conference co-hosted by Norad and the Centre for Global Development and held in Oslo, Norway from 24-25 October 2023.
Specific Objective 3: Enhance the capacity of African universities to train graduate students.
Since its establishment, African universities have been CODESRIAs main constituency. Building the capacity of these universities to train graduate students is therefore a key objective of CODESRIA in the 2023-2027 strategic planning cycle. To achieve this, CODESRIA has adopted a strategy of using individual researchers and faculty in universities as the entry point into enhancing the capacity of those universities to train graduate students.
Gender Institute Reflections meeting: CODESRIA convened its annual Gender Institute in Kampala Uganda, on the 7th 9th June 2023 under the theme CODESRIAs Experience with Gender Research: Towards a Feminist Epistemic Breakthrough? The Institute was co-hosted with the College of Humanities and Social Sciences and the School of Women and Gender Studies at Makerere University (MAK).
Democratic Governance Institute Reflections meeting: The Council convened the 2023 Democratic Governance Institute as a reflections meeting aimed at taking stock of the Institutes 30-year contribution to the study of democratic governance and charting a new trajectory for its future. Held from 5th 7th July 2023 in Lomé, Togo on the theme Africas Experiences with Democratic Governance: A Reflection informed by CODESRIAs Democratic Governance Institute, 1992-2022, the meeting drew a cross section of participants including past laureates, key policy practitioners and leading democratic governance scholars.
College of Mentors: The College of Mentors is part of CODESRIAs ongoing efforts to broaden its interventions and strengthen social sciences and humanities scholarship in African universities.
Diaspora Visiting Fellowships: launched in 2019, the visiting fellowships is an initiative that seeks to mobilise the African academic diaspora to support African universities in order to strengthen teaching, research and knowledge production in the social sciences and humanities through a collaborative approach with academics based at an African university.
Advanced Senior Grants for higher Education Studies: the selection of recipients of this grant took place in the last quarter of 2023.
Drive for Democracy: The Council hosted the first of two convenings seeking to support the praxis and scholarship of academic freedom in Africa towards deepening democratic values in the wider society. The first convening was held in November 2023 in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania in collaboration with the College for Social Sciences, University of Dar es Salaam. The second convening is set to be held in Mozambique in April 2024 in collaboration with Eduardo Mondlane University. The Council hopes that these convenings will provide the overarching framework to revisit the Dar es Salaam and Kampala declarations on Academic Freedom and Social Responsibility while providing a platform for the exchange of transformative ideas and evidence-based advocacy for, among other things, academic freedom and democracy in the Africa. The 2023 Dar es Salaam convening brought together participants from universities (staff unions and student bodies), government, and the civil society. The launch of the second edition of Issa Shivjis book The Concept of Human Rights in Africa published by CODESRIA was also held on the back of this meeting. A recommendation to revisit the Kampala Declaration and to revitalize the Academic Freedom Programme at CODESRIA was also adopted.
Specific Objective 4: Strengthen the capacity for institutional effectiveness and accountability.
CODESRIA continued to make strides in increasing its effectiveness and creating institutional structures for programme delivery in an accountable manner. These efforts covered a wide range of areas, including human resources, facilities and equipment, internal policies, resource mobilization, post-audit action plan and the election of a new Executive Committee.
Human resources: the 2023-2027 strategic plan allowed CODESRIA to reimagine its organogram to more efficiently achieve its goals. While funding in 2023 did not allow the Council to fill in all the vacant positions, CODESRIA was able to recruit the first set of senior and middle level staff in 2023, with the second round of recruitments set for 2024. The recruitments done in 2023 were for a Senior Programme Officer, 2 programme officers and a programme manager. The Council was unable to do a full scale recruitment in part due to the uncertainty around securing a long-term grant from Sida. The scheduled recruitments for 2024 are based on the final stages of a funding partnership discussions with Mastercard Foundation. This partnership has an initial phase of 3 years and a long term period of up to 10 years.
Facilities and equipment: CODESRIA continued its investment in improving its infrastructural facilities to permit staff to work in conditions to ensure their wellbeing and improve their effectiveness.
Resource mobilization: The Council sought to diversify its funding not only to meet the increasing demands for support from the community it serves but to also provide a stable base against the uncertainties of the current global funding environment. Sida has over the years been the most committed partner of CODESRIA and the Council continued its effort to reinforce this relationship in a situation where Sida had previously raised significant concerns over the Councils administration and management. In October 2023, Sida and CODESRIA signed a cost extension to the agreement on core support. The agreement is valid through to December 2024 with the cumulative funding that was earmarked for 2023 being SEK 10 million. In November 2022, CODESRIA entered into a core funding agreement with Norad of NOK50 million for the period 2022 to 2026. 2023 was the first full year of implementation.
Additionally, the Council initiated conversations and submitted proposals to Open Society Foundation (OSF) and Mastercard Foundation. Both initiatives were successful resulting in the securing of a USD500,000 grant from OSF to support work on advocacy for reparations in Africa. The conversations with Mastercard Foundation resulted in approval of the agreement but has not been signed due to two concerns. The first is review of CODESRIAs tax obligations and the second, the need to open a separate dollar account in Dakar for this funding. It is anticipated that the Council will finalise this process in the first quarter of 2024.
Post-audit action plan: CODESRIA achieved significant accomplishment in implementing recommendations contained in the post-audit action plan. In May and September 2023, relevant updates were made to the action plan to ensure that progress made was adequately documented.
Election of the Executive Committee (EC): The postponement of the GA to December 2023 also had implications on the governance structures of the Council. For the first time in CODESRIAs history, the EC elected in the 2018 GA served beyond its stipulated term. While this did not impact the operations of the Council, correcting this anomaly was priority thus the elections of the new EC took place on the final day (8th December) of the General Assembly. As is established in the CODESRIA Charter, each sub-region of the African continent is represented in the Executive Committee by two members. Each sub-region also has one elected alternate member on stand-by to fill any vacancies that may arise in the Executive Committee for any reason whatsoever between General Assemblies.
Specific objective 5: To increase the consideration of gender in the life and work of CODESRIA
CODESRIA has for long considered gender to be important in terms of its intellectual agenda as well as the composition of the Councils governance structures. The retention of gender as one of the cross-cutting themes in the Councils 2023-2027 strategic plan was therefore deliberate. Over the period under review, the Council achieved the following milestones to realize its goals of ensuring the consideration of gender in its life and work.
In April 2023, the Council held a two-day Policy Forum in Dakar, Senegal for the final phase of activities from the 2019 Ford Foundation funded project on Women, Girls and Civic Engagement in Africa and the 2020/2021 Gender and Democratic Governance Institutes. Furthermore, the election of Lyn Ossome as the new President of CODESRIA marks the sixth time in the 50-year history of the Council that a female member of the African academy has occupied that position in the leadership of the Council.
Deliberate efforts were taken to emphasize the desirability of female applicants in all calls for applications issued in 2023. In addition, the special MRI special call for female scholars is part of a set of measures implemented to build upon past achievements and markedly increase the involvement of female scholars in the activities and governance of CODESRIA during the 2023-2027 strategic cycle. Furthermore, in the Mastercard Foundation proposal, the Council makes a commitment to ensure that 70 per cent of participants in the project are female.
